scope: Only the analytic evaluation of the explicit radialized iterated Haar/spatial integral on the right of the first equality in Ex60, through its second equality and the ensuing B6 specialization Eq21. This does NOT identify this integral with H(lambda), prove a Gaussian density law, justify radialization of the original signed mixture, or perform Fubini on the original experiment. Those are separately excluded source obligations.

sealed_proposal_signatures.radialized_test_integral:
theorem radialized_test_integral {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 ≤ ℓ) :
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let U : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0
    let a : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * U O
    let p : ℝ := (n : ℝ) / 2
    (∀ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) volume) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det *
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4))) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * U O - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) / (a O) ^ p) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det *
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) ∂orthogonalHaar n) /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ p =
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (Real.sqrt κ - 1) ^ (n - 1) / (2 : ℝ) ^ p) *
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
          ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * U O - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n)

sealed_meaning_definitions.singleBlockPrecision: Literal source Eq4 existing real precision ((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T).
sealed_meaning_definitions.orthogonalHaar: Existing concrete full O(n) Borel probability Measure.haarMeasure(top), both determinant signs; its probability/compactness facts are internally proved.
sealed_meaning_definitions.EuclideanSpace: Canonical finite real Euclidean space on Fin n and its canonical volume; all powers with real exponent p=n/2 are Real.rpow, not integer division.
sealed_meaning_definitions.local_lets: j0 is source coordinate1 represented as Fin n coordinate0; U=O00; a(O)=kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U; p=(n:R)/2. All are literal local abbreviations, not hypotheses.

nodes.statement: For the generic B6 argument, h is an arbitrary Borel function on the real line with E|h(U)|<infinity. This is a premise of the already stated B6 theorem, not a new premise of the proposed radialized_test_integral theorem.
n is a natural dimension with n>=3; kappa is real with kappa>=4; O has normalized Haar law on the full O(n); lambda is real with lambda>=0.
A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T).
U=O_11; p=n/2 is real division; write a(O)=kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U.
Full O(n) is a compact topological group; its normalized Borel Haar measure is a probability and is invariant under left multiplication, including determinant-minus-one row reflections.
Orthogonality implies |U|<=1 and |det O|=1; U and det are continuous.
a(O)>=kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)=2+4lambda>=2>0. The source calls the denominator at least 2+4lambda; mathematically this is the base a before exponentiation.
For positive bases, real powers obey multiplication, quotient, and exponent-addition rules. p=n/2>0; a^p>0; a^(-p)=1/a^p. In particular 2^(2p)=2^n (real power agrees with natural power at n).

Use B6 with a Borel real scalar h whose restriction to [-1,1] is (kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)u)^(-p). A Borel extension outside this interval suffices; for example compose this positive-base formula with clamp to [-1,1]. Source does not spell out the extension. On the actual U this is precisely 1/a(O)^p.
h(U) is measurable and |h(U)|<= (2+4lambda)^(-p)<=2^(-p). Probability Haar then gives E|h(U)|<infinity, satisfying B6's actual admissibility premise without placing it in the new theorem's binders.
With s=sqrt(kappa), B_t=(s+1)I-tO and b=s-1, A_O=(1/4)B_b^T B_b.
For 0<=t<=sqrt(kappa)-1, ||B_t v|| >= (sqrt(kappa)+1-t)||v|| >= 2||v||.
B_t is invertible by the displayed lower bound. det B_0=(sqrt(kappa)+1)^n>0 and continuous nonvanishing det B_t stays positive on the interval.
sqrt(det A_O)=2^(-n) det((sqrt(kappa)+1)I-(sqrt(kappa)-1)O). Taking square roots uses positivity of det B_b, not merely det(B_b)^2.
det(O)sqrt(det A_O)=2^(-n)det((sqrt(kappa)+1)O-(sqrt(kappa)-1)I), by multiplication with O^T and transpose invariance of determinant.
For S subset {1,...,n}, O_{S,S} is its principal submatrix; det O_empty=1, det O_{ {1},{1} }=U.
|det O_{S,S}|<=1 for every principal minor. This bound is stated without its proof; standard proof uses Hadamard's inequality and row norms of an orthogonal matrix.
For Borel h with E|h(U)|<infinity, every det O_{S,S} h(U) is measurable and absolutely integrable, dominated by |h(U)|. This justifies genuine signed expectations and finite-sum linearity.
If i>=2 lies in S, D_i=I-2e_i e_i^T satisfies D_i O equal in law to O, (D_i O)_11=U, and det((D_i O)_{S,S})=-det O_{S,S}.
Haar invariance and row reflection show E[det O_{S,S}h(U)]=-E[det O_{S,S}h(U)], hence zero whenever S includes an index >=2.

Expand det((sqrt(kappa)+1)O-(sqrt(kappa)-1)I) as sum_S (sqrt(kappa)+1)^|S| (-(sqrt(kappa)-1))^(n-|S|) det O_{S,S}, and take expectations. Standard determinant multilinearity supplies the expansion; source displays the expected expansion.
Only S=empty and S={1} survive, yielding 2^(-n)[(-(sqrt(kappa)-1))^n E h(U)+(sqrt(kappa)+1)(-(sqrt(kappa)-1))^(n-1) E U h(U)].
For every Borel h with E|h(U)|<infinity, E[det(O)sqrt(det A_O)h(U)] = ((-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^n) E[((sqrt(kappa)+1)U-(sqrt(kappa)-1))h(U)].

O -> det O sqrt(det A_O) is continuous: matrix entries, determinant and real sqrt are continuous. Compact O(n) makes its absolute value bounded by a finite constant C. This compactness argument suffices for outer integrability without constructing any Gaussian law.
For each real a>0, the Euclidean Lebesgue integral of exp(-a||x||^2/4) equals (4pi/a)^p and is absolutely integrable.

Standard Euclidean Gaussian integral includes measurability and finite nonnegative integral; it follows by one-dimensional Gaussian integration and product Lebesgue measure in an orthonormal coordinate system (or radial integration). This standard analytic result is not proved in the source.
For every O, exp(-a(O)||x||^2/4) is Integrable over canonical volume on real Euclidean n-space.
J(O)=integral_x exp(-a(O)||x||^2/4)=(4pi/a(O))^p=(4pi)^p/a(O)^p.

The literal signed outer integrand det(O)sqrt(det A_O) J(O) is measurable and absolutely integrable: |weight J|<= C (4pi)^p 2^(-p), a finite constant on probability Haar. This is a substantive Integrable fact, not Lean's default value for a divergent integral.
The determinant-weighted denominator quotient det(O)sqrt(det A_O)/a(O)^p is absolutely integrable, by the same bounded weight and denominator estimates.

Since a>0 and pi>0, (4pi/a)^p/(2pi)^p=2^p/a^p. Moving the fixed positive finite scalar through the genuine integrable outer expectation gives I=2^p E[det(O)sqrt(det A_O)/a(O)^p], where I is exactly the normalized explicit radial iterated integral.
N(O)=(sqrt(kappa)+1)U-(sqrt(kappa)-1) is continuous and |N(O)|<=2sqrt(kappa), since sqrt(kappa)>=2 and |U|<=1.
N(O)/a(O)^p is measurable and absolutely integrable, dominated by 2sqrt(kappa) 2^(-p) on probability Haar.
The actual B6 theorem with h(U)=1/a(O)^p gives E[det(O)sqrt(det A_O)/a(O)^p]=((-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^n) E[N(O)/a(O)^p].
Combine the factor 2^p from Gaussian normalization and 2^(-n) from B6. As n=2p, 2^p/2^n=2^(-p), yielding exactly (-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^p.
I=((-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^p) E[N(O)/a(O)^p]. This transports Eq21's RHS to the explicit radial integral only; it asserts no equality to the original H(lambda).
Conjoin each-inner Integrable, literal-outer Integrable, final-quotient Integrable, and scoped_identity, under exactly n>=3,kappa>=4,lambda>=0.
